verdict: ExxonMobil's profit doubled to $14.5B as sales jumped 44% to $114.5B on much higher oil and gas prices, with every segment earning more than a year ago.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Sales and other operating revenue of $114.5B, up from $79.5B a year ago; total revenue including other income was $116.0B

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Up from $1.64 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $3.52

kpis.label: Energy Products earnings
kpis.note: Refining and fuels earnings (GAAP), up from $1.4B a year ago as refining margins jumped

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: Cash flow from operations was $23.6B; $9.4B was returned to shareholders in dividends and buybacks

segments.name: Upstream
segments.note: Oil and gas production — crude and gas sold to outside buyers. Most output goes to ExxonMobil's own refineries, so earnings are the better gauge: $7.9B, up from $5.4B a year ago, on production of 4,514 thousand barrels of oil-equivalent a day.

segments.name: Energy Products
segments.note: Refining and fuels — gasoline, diesel and jet fuel sold worldwide, by far the largest sales line. Earnings jumped to $5.5B from $1.4B a year ago as refining margins surged (the indicative margin was $29.0 a barrel, vs $16.3 in Q1).

segments.name: Chemical Products
segments.note: Basic chemicals and plastics that go into packaging, cars and everyday goods. Earnings were $1.1B, up from $293M a year ago on a North American feedstock advantage.

segments.name: Specialty Products
segments.note: Higher-value products — lubricants, basestocks and specialty fluids. Earnings rose to $956M from $780M a year ago on higher basestock margins.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Sales and other operating revenue in Corporate and Financing that is not part of a reportable segment — the small remainder so the segments add up to the company total.

flow.costPlain: Crude oil and product purchases ($67,801M) plus production and manufacturing expenses ($12,250M) — what it costs ExxonMobil to buy, pump and process oil and gas.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative expenses
opex.note: Sales teams, offices and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation and depletion
opex.note: The cost of wells, refineries and plants wearing out over time, including impairments.

opex.name: Other taxes and duties
opex.note: Taxes and duties on products and operations — separate from income tax.

opex.name: Exploration expenses
opex.note: Searching for new oil and gas, including dry holes.

opex.name: Non-service pension and postretirement benefit expense
opex.note: Pension and retiree-benefit costs outside service cost.

otherDetail: Income from equity affiliates of $893M plus other income of $595M, less the $356M of net income attributable to noncontrolling interests — outside partners' shares of joint ventures — leaving $1,132M.
footerNote: Revenue is sales and other operating revenue; equity and other income are shown as other income in the flow.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Prices did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Brent crude averaged $104.52 a barrel in the quarter (the U.S. marker, WTI, $93.21), and ExxonMobil's own U.S. crude realized $97.58. Sales rose 44% while production of 4,514 thousand oil-equivalent barrels a day was the highest in more than two decades, excluding Middle East disruptions.

takeaways.title: Refining quadrupled its earnings
takeaways.text: Energy Products earned $5,465M, up from $1,366M a year ago, as refining margins surged and diesel production hit a second-quarter record. Upstream added $7,927M, helped by record Permian output above 1.8 million barrels a day.

takeaways.title: Cash kept flowing back
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $23.6B and free cash flow $17.2B. ExxonMobil returned $9.4B to shareholders ($4.3B of dividends, $5.1B of buybacks) and declared a third-quarter dividend of $1.03 a share.

oneTimers: GAAP earnings include $1,079M of impairments among the company's 'identified items,' plus other identified charges including $1,365M added to financial reserves. Excluding identified items and timing effects, adjusted earnings were $14,680M, or $3.52 a share — only slightly above GAAP, because favorable timing effects offset much of the charges.

Results were delivered despite Middle East disruptions that took part of upstream production offline; a fifth Guyana floating production vessel is on plan to start up in Q4 2026, adding 250 thousand barrels a day of capacity.
